source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed on the withdrawal of Mr. W. H. Smith: 'Mr. W. H. Smith ... yesterday withdrew his nomination ..., and Major William Stewart, M.C., J.P., the retiring Unionist member, was returned unopposed' (Belfast News-Letter, 26 April 1933) Original citation restored 6 Nov 2026 (the 5 Nov verification had moved it because of a text-cleaning fault).

note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1933. Polling took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933: 'The voting in the Local Government Elections in Tyrone took place on Wednesday and passed without incident. There was one County Council contest, that in Killeter division of Castlederg Union' (Ulster Herald, 3 June 1933, p. 5). The Belfast News-Letter of 26 April 1933, p. 6 likewise reports the Clogher withdrawal and says 'There will thus be only one contest for County Council honours in the Nationalist division of Killeter.' Killeter: Denis O'Kane (Nat.) 635, Francis M'Laughlin (Nat.) 293, majority 342, total poll 932, 5 spoiled (Ulster Herald, 3 June 1933, p. 5; Irish News, 2 June 1933, p. 5). Clogher: Major William Stewart (U.) returned unopposed on the withdrawal of Mr. W. H. Smith (Belfast News-Letter, 26 April 1933, p. 6). The other 25 divisions are recorded from the Mid-Ulster Mail's full list of the nominations (22 April 1933, p. 6, page image read): 22 single nominations, returned unopposed, and Cookstown, Coagh and Strabane, where no nomination was lodged and the retiring members continued to sit. Labels are as printed. (The earlier reconstruction of these 25 from the 1939 list is replaced; five of its names differ from the 1933 list.) Described in the report as 'the retiring Unionist member'; no party label is printed beside the name. Returned unopposed.
